A FEW THINGS TO UNDERSTAND ABOUT THE AI SELL-OFF 💡

The last few weeks have been rough for anyone invested in AI stocks.

NVIDIA - which I am not invested in - is almost 40% below its October high, and Micron and TSMC have dropped 24% and 16% in a month. This is obviously not fun to watch, but stocks cannot go up uninterrupted, and to be honest I prefer this to a meltup with stocks flying up, followed by a bubble bursting.

For now, this is much more controlled, although the $SPX500  has now entered correction territory and we have had a fair number of red days recently. We have to remember, though, that this follows three years of double-digit returns in the market.

There are real reasons for the nervousness in the market:

- Interest rates are rising. The Fed hiked rates in September for the first time since 2023, and the 10-year yield is above 5%. A fair share of the AI buildout is now financed with debt, and the weakest borrowers feel it first. CoreWeave's unsecured bonds yield around 16%. This is something to watch, and I take it seriously.

- Democrats won the midterms. Washington matters less than the headlines suggest, because Trump still has his veto. The real effect is local. Texas elected a governor who campaigned pausing for new data centers, and Texas alone accounts for roughly a quarter of the capacity planned in the US.

- Jensen Huang left Nvidia. He resigned last week with immediate effect, and the company has no permanent CEO. Nobody knows who will run the most important company in AI a year from now.

So the buildout can be delayed. Some data centers will be built later, in other places, and with more expensive financing, but a delay is not a lack of demand.

Look at what the companies reported amid all this:

Nvidia's first quarter without Jensen 𝘀𝗵𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗱𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗮 𝘆𝗲𝗮𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗼, and the company raised its growth target for next fiscal year to 75%. TSMC had record revenue in October, up almost 60%. Micron has already sold more than 75% of everything it can produce in 2027. And Microsoft lowered its spending plan this year for one reason: its partners couldn't deliver capacity fast enough.

So the main problem is demand that the industry cannot keep up with, and based on that, I think the recent sell-off is an overreaction by the market, including what we are seeing today.

Over the last few years, I have seen my own work change. Three years ago, I used AI chatbots for simple things like answering questions. Then I started experimenting with coding and other things, and today I have AI agents that write code, test strategies, read earnings reports for me, and make sentiment gauges, and I am using 100x more tokens than I did back then. Next year, I am sure I will use 10x more, and I think many others will start using AI as I do now over the next years. It is basically the new operating system for your computer, and I have not met anyone who started working this way and then went back to using AI less.

In short, AI is developing at an explosive pace, and companies will have to deliver it to consumers in one way or another because demand isn't going to disappear.

Right now, 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗰𝗸 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗳𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴. That gap cannot stay open forever, and over the next few quarters, I believe earnings reports will close it. The price trend in many AI stocks is clearly negative, and a negative trend can last longer than one earnings season. However, I believe fundamentals will win out over sentiment in the end, so I am staying invested, and I have used the weakness to add to my positions in AMD, Micron and TSMC, as I believe these are attractive long-term opportunities. Pullbacks like this are part of investing in a strong trend, and this is the price you pay as an investor for the long-term privilege of compounding your investments over time.

So while the market is selling the AI stocks big time right now, I am happy to take the other side of this trade. It may take some time to prove that this is the right thing to do though. But I have the time 😊

Thank you for following and copying 🙏
